samples.summary: Parity guard only covers `./store/block-helpers.js`; other value exports the Node-resolved integration lane depends on can still drift and fail at import time
samples.evidence: `const SOURCE = './store/block-helpers.js'` and the `if (match[2] !== SOURCE) continue;` filter mean the test only compares that one source module. But `packages/frontend/tests/**/*.integration.ts` runs under `tsx --test` (packages/frontend/package.json:16), which resolves `@wafflebase/docs` through the `node` export condition to `dist/node.js`, and the modules loaded there import many other *value* symbols from the package: `resolvePageSetup`, `normalizeBlockStyle`, `DEFAULT_BLOCK_STYLE`, `blockStyleId`, `materializeBlockSpacing` (packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:27-41), `getBlockText`, `resolveOffset` (packages/frontend/src/app/docs/comments/docs-anchor.ts:1-4), `generateBlockId`, `createTableBlock` (tests/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store-concurrent.integration.ts:14). All happen to be present in src/node.ts today, so nothing is broken now — but the exact failure mode this test was written to catch (a symbol exported only from `src/index.ts`) remains unguarded for `model/types.js` and `model/named-styles.js`, which is where most of those symbols come from.
searchedFor: read packages/docs/src/node.ts and src/index.ts export lists

samples.summary: Export-clause parser treats inline `type` specifiers as value names, which can produce a false parity failure
samples.evidence: `clause.trim().split(/\s+as\s+/).pop()` returns `Bar` for a clause written `type Bar` and the `type` keyword is never stripped. If someone writes `export { foo, type Bar } from './store/block-helpers.js'` in `src/index.ts` while `src/node.ts` re-exports `Bar` via its separate `export type { ... } from './store/block-helpers.js'` line (which the regex deliberately skips, node.ts:115), the test reports a missing export that is in fact present. Cosmetic today since neither entry mixes inline type specifiers into the block-helpers value clause.
